C031.notes: SER OC-AU-001. George VI · IND:IMP still in legend (Emperor of India — pre-1948 drop). Reverse: three wheat stalks · AUSTRALIA · THREE PENCE · 1943 · S. Country #10. Wartime: Australia needed silver change, US mints helped. Pocket money from a Pacific-war economy — melt, not face. Junk Ag = melt (see SILVER.md). SER siblings: OC-AU-002 (1944 Perth penny) · OC-AU-003 (1966 platypus 20¢). Australia flips now 3.
C031.story: A 1943 Australian threepence, struck in the middle of World War II. King George VI is on the front, and the back shows three stalks of wheat by George Kruger Gray, a design used since 1938 — before the war began. It's made of real silver, which is why it feels different from today's coins in your hand.

C114.notes: SER NA-MX-001. User shorthand 1914 + photo — and this one earns the long card. 1914 Chihuahua copper struck for the Ejército Constitucionalista while Francisco Villa’s División del Norte held the north: the old Chihuahua mint’s leftover presses, quiet since 1895, suddenly among the best-struck coinage of the whole Revolution. Engravers J. Salazar and M. Revilla cut the dies; Walrafen later mapped dozens of die marriages — common in absolute terms, endlessly variable up close. The copper itself is the story collectors retell from Fehrenbach: torn from telegraph and telephone wire across the vast Luis Terrazas estates after villistas seized the latifundio — wires that once carried a cattle baron’s messages, melted into pocket change for an army. Same calendar year Europe marched into WWI; in Chihuahua the Constitucionalista legend and a sword through a 5 bought tortillas and cartridges. First Mexico flip in this vault (silver Libertad is B007). Was once oldest flip (now Switzerland 1883 C242 / EU-CH-001). SER siblings: NA-MX-002…NA-MX-009. Mexico flips now 9.
C114.story: A 1914 5-centavo coin from Mexico. The front shows a liberty cap with rays and the words REPUBLICA MEXICANA and E. DE CHIHA. The back shows a large 5 pierced by an upright arrow, a centavo monogram, the words EJERCITO CONSTITUCIONALISTA and 1914, and often the name SALAZAR. Made of copper.

C262.story: A 1984 1 dinar from Yugoslavia. The obverse shows SFRY arms (torch and wheat); the reverse shows big 1; bilingual ДИНАР / DINAR legend, date, beaded rim. Struck in nickel-brass.

C282.notes: Phase 1 from the value side only (owner photo).
C282.story: A 1965 fifty-para coin from Yugoslavia. The side shown has a large 50 in a beaded circle, with the word para in the country's languages and Cyrillic and Latin letters around it, and the date split as 19 and 65.

lots.denom_text: 1 troy oz rounds × 7 (no face · private mint Buffalo / Indian Head type)
lots.notes: User shorthand 7 oz buffalos + photo. Classic stacker design — Indian Head / Buffalo nickel homage — but these are rounds, not legal-tender Eagles. Seven full troy ounces of .999 that never needed a Whitman year slot. Valued as generic bullion (melt + light product), not the ASE calendar premium in SILVER.md. Vault Ag jumps ~26.438 → ~33.438 oz.
lots.storage_text: clear plastic tube (capacity ~20) · 7 rounds photographed fanned

lots.composition_text: .999 fine Ag · 1.000 oz · Type 1 Walking Liberty / Mercanti heraldic eagle · BU · loose with Mint tube bits
lots.denom_text: $1 ASE · 1 troy oz
lots.notes: User shorthand 1 extra 2019 silver eagle. Duplicate year — A026 already seats 2019 in the Whitman calendar. This one lives as a flip: same common-date premium as the album twin, not a second hole fill. Type 1, last stretch before the 2021 redesign. Vault ASE count now 25 oz (24 in albums + this extra).
lots.storage_text: loose · green US Mint tube cap + white tube fragment in photo

lots.composition_text: .999 fine Ag · ASW 10.000 oz · in original orange retail box
lots.denom_text: 10 troy oz cast/poured bar (window shows embossed 9 on face)
lots.notes: User shorthand 10 oz bar silver + photo. Ten ounces in one brick — the densest single card in the flips. Not an Eagle, not a Buffalo round: just weight with a brand on the sleeve. Vault Ag ~34.438 → ~44.438 oz. Soft beat 1500 is in sight from metal alone.
lots.storage_text: orange Fine Mint box · “10 TROY OUNCES · .999 FINE SILVER”

lots.composition_text: .9999 fine Ag · BU · radial lines visible through retail flip
lots.denom_text: $5 CAD face · 1 troy oz Maple Leaf
lots.notes: Not a white 2×2 flip — bullion sleeve. First Canada metal card. RCM Maple with security radials, still in the Nov 2023 APMEX bag. Sister weight to the ASE / Buffalo / Fine Mint stack. Vault Ag ~44.438 → ~45.438 oz.
lots.storage_text: APMEX bag + clear retail flip · “2023 Canada 1 oz Silver Maple Leaf BU” · 258888 / 1-2-5 · 11/07/23

Britannia still holds the shield; the crown just changed hands. UK already on the flip board (decimal bronze); this is the weight card. Vault Ag ~45.438 → ~46.438 oz.

lots.composition_text: .999 silver proofs (dime · 2× quarters · half) + clad/Mn-brass proofs (1¢ · 5¢ · $1) · OGP lenses + sleeve · proof
lots.denom_text: 7-coin United States Mint Silver Proof Set®
lots.notes: Contents: Lincoln 1¢ · Jefferson 5¢ · Ag Roosevelt 10¢ · Ag Tuskegee Airmen quarter (last ATB) · Ag Washington Crossing the Delaware quarter (one-year type) · Ag Kennedy 50¢ · Native American $1 (military service reverse · not silver). Mirror fields, frosted devices, San Francisco S. Issue was $105 — valued near melt + light OGP, not dealer ask. A sealed little 2021: last park quarter, a one-year Delaware crossing, and Kennedy still in silver while the dollar stayed brass. Lives under Sets, not flips. Ag known now ~2.438 oz.
lots.storage_text: original US Mint packaging (black sleeve · Washington Monument art · two lenses)

lots.composition_text: CuNi clad + bronze 1¢ · no silver · proof cameo · OGP black case · red insert · black sleeve
lots.denom_text: 6-coin United States Proof Set (1¢ · 5¢ · 10¢ · 25¢ · 50¢ · SBA $1)
lots.notes: First SBA dollar year in a proof set — Eisenhower’s replacement still brand-new in 1979. Type I is the common filled-S; Type II clear-S is the chase. Clad sandwich through the half — this is proof polish and OGP, not melt. Companion to S001 (2021-S silver). Lives under Sets.
lots.storage_text: original US Mint packaging (black cardboard sleeve · black plastic case · red flocking) · light sleeve wear
